Caroline A. Crenshaw discusses the challenges and risks associated with SPACs, acknowledging their recent popularity and proposing new rules to enhance investor protections and transparency in SPAC transactions.

d1bf5849c10668f90ebf3f9c.title: Statement on Staff Bulletin on Account Recommendations to Retail Investors
d1bf5849c10668f90ebf3f9c.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: Gary Gensler addressed the release of an SEC Staff Bulletin emphasizing the obligations of broker-dealers and investment advisers to prioritize the best interests of retail investors under applicable regulations.

9c43af6291ac993ac240138a.title: Statement on Proposal on Special Purpose Acquisition Companies (SPACs), Shell Companies, and Projections
9c43af6291ac993ac240138a.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: SEC Chair Gary Gensler supports a proposal to enhance investor protections for special purpose acquisition companies (SPACs) by strengthening disclosure requirements, marketing standards, and gatekeeper obligations, ensuring investors receive protections akin to those of traditional IPOs.

5034c19ca555f8cc39da5011.title: Statement on the Proposal to Enhance Investor Protections in SPACs
5034c19ca555f8cc39da5011.speaker: Allison Herren

enrichment.summary: The SEC, led by Allison Herren, proposes amendments to enhance investor protections in SPACs due to rapid growth and associated risks for retail investors. Key changes include increased transparency regarding sponsor compensation and accountability for SPAC transactions.

790bc82634441f791e0a22ea.title: Damning and Deeming: Dissenting Statement on Shell Companies, Projections, and SPACs Proposal
790bc82634441f791e0a22ea.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce expresses dissent regarding SEC's proposal on SPACs, criticizing it for imposing burdens that deter SPACs instead of enhancing disclosures. She advocates for investor empowerment through better disclosures rather than regulatory constraints.

7428122f2ec59a9845db42f3.title: Remarks at the ICI Investment Management Conference
7428122f2ec59a9845db42f3.speaker: William Birdthistle

enrichment.summary: William Birdthistle emphasizes the crucial role of investment funds in the U.S. economy, advocating for better transparency and investor engagement while celebrating the advantages of collective investment vehicles.

4edcc74b26d6ae5d2528babb.title: Statement on the Further Definition of a Dealer-Trader
4edcc74b26d6ae5d2528babb.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: SEC proposes rules to define dealers, enhancing registration for firms involved in providing liquidity in securities markets, particularly around Treasury securities. The initiative aims to ensure market stability and investor protection by requiring significant market participants to register.

533d33e8cb032defd4b79243.title: Statement on Proposal to Further Define “As a Part of a Regular Business” in the Definition of Dealer and Government Securities Dealer
533d33e8cb032defd4b79243.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce discusses a proposal intended to clarify the definition of 'dealer' under the Exchange Act, focusing on the challenges arising from non-registered liquidity providers in the market. While acknowledging the need for clarity, she expresses reservations about the proposal's breadth and potential impact on market liquidity, resilience, and regulatory complexities.

203260654fe1da5f83be4aad.title: Statement on Proposal to Remove References of Credit Ratings from Regulation M
203260654fe1da5f83be4aad.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: The SEC proposes removing credit rating references from Regulation M to fulfill a Congressional mandate from the Dodd-Frank Act, aimed at enhancing market integrity post-2008 financial crisis.

ae4ea164ee5fd6b7b4ad2f34.title: Statement on Jury’s Verdict in Trial of Ambassador Advisors, LLC, Bernard I. Bostwick, Robert E. Kauffman, and Adrian E. Young
ae4ea164ee5fd6b7b4ad2f34.speaker: Gurbir S. Grewal

enrichment.summary: The SEC announced a jury verdict in favor of the agency against Bernard I. Bostwick, Robert E. Kauffman, and Adrian E. Young, holding them accountable for breaching fiduciary duties related to mutual fund share class selection. The verdict highlights the agency's commitment to enforcing fiduciary responsibilities of investment advisers.

b3bb59be3003b9837f4299a7.title: Statement on Jury’s Verdict in Trial of Jonathan Dax Cooke and Keystone Capital Partners
b3bb59be3003b9837f4299a7.speaker: Gurbir S. Grewal

enrichment.summary: The SEC is pleased with the jury's verdict in favor of the agency against Jonathan Dax Cooke and Keystone Capital Partners for fraudulently selling variable annuities to federal employees nearing retirement, misrepresenting themselves as government counselors.

29890ad60bab81571c40c0bb.title: Statement on Proposed Mandatory Climate Risk Disclosures
29890ad60bab81571c40c0bb.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: SEC Chair Gary Gensler advocates for a proposed mandate on climate-risk disclosures for public companies, highlighting its potential to provide investors with essential, comparable information and improve corporate transparency regarding climate-related financial risks.

037b667b439db928197f664e.title: We are Not the Securities and Environment Commission - At Least Not Yet
037b667b439db928197f664e.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: In her speech, Hester M. Peirce criticizes the SEC's proposal for mandatory climate disclosures, arguing it undermines existing frameworks and lacks a clear rationale. She highlights the proposal's potential to distort materiality, impose high costs, and hurt investors and the economy, while questioning the Commission's authority and expertise in this area.

entities.name: Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures

f14ebd257390a5e479eaaeae.title: Statement on the Enhancement and Standardization of Climate-Related Disclosures for Investors
f14ebd257390a5e479eaaeae.speaker: Caroline A. Crenshaw

enrichment.summary: The SEC emphasizes the need for standardized climate-related disclosures to empower investors and enhance transparency in financial reporting. The proposal aims to modernize existing frameworks and improve the reliability of climate risk data, making it essential for investors' decision-making.

519d634c282349fd1cfd20d1.title: Shelter from the Storm: Helping Investors Navigate Climate Change Risk[1]
519d634c282349fd1cfd20d1.speaker: Allison Herren

enrichment.summary: In a speech to investors, Allison Herren emphasizes the SEC's proposal for enhanced disclosure of climate change risks, highlighting its urgency and the responsibility of the Commission to ensure that investors have adequate information to assess and manage risks associated with climate change. The proposal aims to standardize disclosures based on established frameworks like TCFD and the GHG Protocol, supporting investor needs for better climate-related information.

entities.name: Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD)

e84c4ff25462881e43a230be.title: Statement on Planned Departure of Commissioner Allison Herren Lee
e84c4ff25462881e43a230be.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: SEC Commissioner Allison Herren Lee announced she will not seek a second term. Gary Gensler praises her dedication and contributions, particularly in climate-related disclosures.

5bfba3676ae5e929c2fcc993.title: Statement on Planned Departure from the Commission
5bfba3676ae5e929c2fcc993.speaker: Allison Herren

enrichment.summary: Commissioner Allison Herren announces her intent to step down from the SEC after her term expires in June 2022. She expresses gratitude for her role and commitment to ongoing work at the Commission.

The SEC's Division of Trading and Markets urges broker-dealers to enhance their risk management practices during periods of market volatility. Key recommendations include collecting margin, monitoring concentrated positions, conducting stress tests, and closely monitoring risk management limits.

055a3d6eb519dd3c2e6f8afc.title: Remarks at Meeting of the SEC Investor Advisory Committee
055a3d6eb519dd3c2e6f8afc.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce addressed the SEC Investor Advisory Committee, recognizing departing members and emphasizing the importance of discussions on ethics in AI services and cyber risk disclosures for investors. She expressed concerns over a proposed rule affecting cyber-security programs and sought input from the panelists.

ef34b74781f956e255e1ab56.title: Prepared Remarks before the Investor Advisory Committee
ef34b74781f956e255e1ab56.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: Gary Gensler's remarks discuss the SEC's engagement with the Investor Advisory Committee regarding regulatory issues, particularly focusing on the ethical implications of artificial intelligence in finance, as well as cybersecurity disclosures for investors. He emphasizes the need for investor protections and the dangers of conflicts of interest in financial platforms.

45af892f8be17d3562ba4ec1.title: Statement in Support of a Multi-Pronged Approach to Cybersecurity
45af892f8be17d3562ba4ec1.speaker: Caroline A. Crenshaw

enrichment.summary: Caroline A. Crenshaw's speech emphasizes the urgent challenges of cybersecurity for businesses, citing its significance to national security and economic health. The SEC proposes enhanced disclosure requirements to improve transparency regarding cyber incidents.

f1d3db2615fcb0407fbebbce.title: Statement on Proposal for Mandatory Cybersecurity Disclosures
f1d3db2615fcb0407fbebbce.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: SEC Chair Gary Gensler supports a proposal for mandatory cybersecurity disclosures by public companies to enhance investor transparency and ensure effective risk assessment.

e41d4e7f2d6fe263e3f6b2c6.title: Dissenting Statement on Cybersecurity Risk Management, Strategy, Governance, and Incident Disclosure Proposal
e41d4e7f2d6fe263e3f6b2c6.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce expresses dissent regarding the SEC's proposal on cybersecurity risk management and disclosure, arguing that it oversteps the Commission's authority and imposes excessive regulation on public companies. She supports the idea of companies disclosing cybersecurity incidents but raises concerns about the framework's detailed requirements and the balance between investor protection and law enforcement cooperation.

8ea258fec8a27d402a9e341e.title: Assessing Materiality: Focusing on the Reasonable Investor When Evaluating Errors
8ea258fec8a27d402a9e341e.speaker: Paul Munter

enrichment.summary: This speech emphasizes the importance of accurate financial reporting and the objective assessment of materiality when correcting errors in financial statements. It outlines the need for transparency, the impact of biases on assessments, and the role of auditors in ensuring compliance with GAAP. The conclusion stresses the need for all stakeholders in financial reporting to prioritize the interests of investors.

e1a7e1c6a6f205dcdfbc4fb7.title: The Shareholder Proposal Rule: A Cornerstone of Corporate Democracy
e1a7e1c6a6f205dcdfbc4fb7.speaker: Renee Jones

enrichment.summary: Renee Jones discusses the importance of the SEC's Shareholder Proposal Rule (Rule 14a-8) and its implications for corporate governance, emphasizing the role of shareholders in proposing changes and the current state of the proxy season.

a17c8e389860b07b2f2a3b12.title:
Send Lawyers, Guns and Money:[1]
(Over-) Zealous Representation by Corporate Lawyers
Remarks at PLI’s Corporate Governance – A Master Class 2022
a17c8e389860b07b2f2a3b12.speaker: Allison Herren

enrichment.summary: Allison Herren's speech emphasizes the need for the SEC to enforce professional conduct standards for corporate lawyers to safeguard investors and ensure transparency in corporate disclosures. It critiques the current inadequate standards and calls for a reevaluation of the responsibilities lawyers have to their clients and the public, especially in light of past regulatory failures.

f86c7f58cfd5acaa401c6590.title: Office Hours with Gary Gensler: Dark Pools, Payment for Order Flow & Market Structure
f86c7f58cfd5acaa401c6590.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: In a speech, SEC Chair Gary Gensler discusses the complexities of stock trading, specifically how orders are often routed to wholesalers rather than exchanges, leading to potential conflicts of interest due to payment for order flow. He emphasizes that while this practice can result in no commission fees, it does not ensure the best execution for investors.

897d4d88882e9b687a3f38fc.title: Remarks at the IAA Investment Adviser Compliance Conference
897d4d88882e9b687a3f38fc.speaker: William Birdthistle

enrichment.summary: William Birdthistle, Director of the SEC's Division of Investment Management, addresses the challenges and opportunities in the investment advisory industry amidst profound market changes, emphasizing the importance of regulation and the role of fiduciaries in protecting investor interests.

34f6de25e26eed4800a67b5c.title: Statement on Rules to Increase Transparency of Short Sale Activity
34f6de25e26eed4800a67b5c.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: The SEC proposed new rules to enhance transparency in short sale activities, aiming to provide the public and regulators with better access to short sale data. This initiative follows directives from Congress after the 2008 financial crisis and includes more stringent reporting requirements for large short positions.

cf03ab251e5e1c0eab51dd79.title: Statement on Proposal to Require Short Position and Short Activity Reporting by Institutional Investment Managers
cf03ab251e5e1c0eab51dd79.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce supports a proposal under Section 929X of the Dodd-Frank Act for public disclosure of short sale information by institutional investors. The proposal aims to enhance transparency concerning short interest and includes requirements for monthly and daily reporting of gross short positions. Peirce invites public comments on the proposed framework and its implications for trading strategies.

3a1cdf643249769230b350c5.title: Statement on the FASB’s Agenda Consultation: Engagement with Investors and Other Stakeholders Vital to Development of High Quality Accounting Standards
3a1cdf643249769230b350c5.speaker: Paul Munter

enrichment.summary: In his statement, Paul Munter emphasizes the crucial role of stakeholder engagement, particularly with investors, in the FASB’s standard-setting process. He highlights the need for improved processes to gather and incorporate feedback, ensure transparency, and prioritize areas like climate-related disclosures and digital assets. Munter urges continual evaluation of standards to reflect evolving business needs and investor concerns.

90be1e910ebd48b8e43faf07.title: Statement on Jury’s Verdict in Trial of Adam Mattessich
90be1e910ebd48b8e43faf07.speaker: Gurbir S. Grewal

enrichment.summary: A jury in the Southern District of New York ruled in favor of the SEC against Adam Mattessich, a former trader at Cantor Fitzgerald, for his involvement in a commission-splitting scheme. The SEC emphasizes the importance of compliance with federal securities laws.

d546e0d0e9edbc6e304d6148.title: Statement on Public Dissemination of Security-Based Swap Transactions
d546e0d0e9edbc6e304d6148.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: The SEC, led by Gary Gensler, emphasizes the need for increased transparency in the security-based swap market following historical issues, notably the 2008 financial crisis. New initiatives include public access to transaction information and registration requirements for market participants to enhance transparency and efficiency.

In her speech, Hester M. Peirce discusses the importance of the PCAOB in ensuring financial transparency and stability within the economy. She emphasizes the cooperative nature of economic contributions by various stakeholders, including auditors, and critiques the PCAOB's structure and potential future challenges, including its role in ESG assurance. Peirce supports the current PCAOB board while cautioning against political influences that may undermine its effectiveness.

670c94aca46eab332738b01d.title: Statement on Settlement with BlockFi Lending LLC
670c94aca46eab332738b01d.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: SEC Commissioner Hester M. Peirce expresses dissent regarding the settlement with BlockFi, questioning the effectiveness of current regulatory approaches in protecting crypto lending customers. She argues that the penalties imposed may not adequately serve investor protection and that a more flexible regulatory framework could facilitate transparency and access to crypto lending products for retail customers.

60339dc4cc0c80dfe59a9133.title: Statement on Amendments to the Whistleblower Program
60339dc4cc0c80dfe59a9133.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: The SEC proposed amendments to enhance its whistleblower program, aiming to incentivize and reward whistleblowers more effectively.

542cd70420319c392556541c.title: Remarks at SEC Small Business Capital Formation Advisory Committee Meeting
542cd70420319c392556541c.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce discusses the need to redefine the accredited investor definition to enhance participation in capital markets for a broader range of investors, particularly emphasizing the challenges faced by founders without generational wealth. Peirce advocates for eliminating wealth and income thresholds in favor of expanding the criteria for accredited investors and highlights recent developments in this area.

c88a13f163a39f4727d3e5fd.title: Remarks Before the Small Business Capital Formation Advisory Committee
c88a13f163a39f4727d3e5fd.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: Gary Gensler addresses the Small Business Capital Formation Advisory Committee, highlighting the importance of the accredited investor definition and its impact on capital raising regulations.

entities.name: Small Business Capital Formation Advisory Committee

enrichment.summary: The SEC proposes to shorten beneficial ownership reporting deadlines, enhancing transparency and reducing information asymmetries in the market.

45c2d0ccb47bf780d1be29e5.title: Statement on Proposal to Revisit Recently Adopted Whistleblower Rule Amendments
45c2d0ccb47bf780d1be29e5.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: In a speech, Hester M. Peirce critiques a proposal to revisit the recently amended whistleblower rules, arguing that there is no compelling reason to do so and that the current rules are functioning effectively. She emphasizes the importance of regulatory consistency and asserts that revisiting these rules may undermine public confidence in the regulatory process.

509f87e7aee0aaf2e03f934c.title: Dissenting Statement on Proposed Modernization of Beneficial Ownership Reporting
509f87e7aee0aaf2e03f934c.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce dissentingly critiques the SEC's proposed amendments to beneficial ownership reporting, arguing they fail to adequately consider market realities and the balance established by the Williams Act. She expresses concerns about the justification for shortening the reporting window from ten to five days, asserting it undermines investor protections and market functioning.

28114c97f2e47a23b5104b60.title: Office Hours with Gary Gensler: Why Do Private Funds Matter?
28114c97f2e47a23b5104b60.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: In his speech, Gary Gensler emphasizes the importance of private funds, like hedge funds and private equity, to everyday investors, particularly through their connections to pension plans and endowments. He discusses the large fees involved in these funds and suggests that increased transparency and competition could benefit both investors and companies seeking growth.

3e18a490eb6d58d8a4e1444c.title: Statement on Cybersecurity Risk Management for Investment Advisers, Registered Investment Companies, and Business Development Companies
3e18a490eb6d58d8a4e1444c.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce from the SEC expresses gratitude for the efforts in developing a cybersecurity proposal but articulates opposition to its framework. She highlights the complexities of cyber threats and suggests that the proposed regulations may unfairly penalize advisers as victims of cybercrime rather than focusing on proactive assistance and cooperation.

497a5c036d06e18fc66b2911.title: Statement on Rules Regarding Clearing and Settling
497a5c036d06e18fc66b2911.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: SEC Chair Gary Gensler supports proposed amendments to the securities clearing and settling process aimed at reducing financial system risk and enhancing market efficiencies. Key proposals include shortening the standard settlement cycle to T+1, mandating prompt confirmations on trade date (T+0), and facilitating automated transaction processing. The speech emphasizes the historical context of settlement cycles and seeks public feedback on further enhancements.

entities.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve

d60030d0a3ecb38a89a483d5.title: Statement on Proposal to Shorten the Settlement Cycle
d60030d0a3ecb38a89a483d5.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce supports the proposal to shorten the settlement cycle from T+2 to T+1, emphasizing the positive impact it could have on reducing settlement risks and costs, especially during high volatility. She invites public comments on further shortening it to T+0, while acknowledging potential challenges.

a54b1fdcd5092e5c0e078ff1.title: Statement on Proposal to Shorten the Standard Settlement Cycle
a54b1fdcd5092e5c0e078ff1.speaker: Allison Herren

enrichment.summary: The SEC proposes to shorten the standard settlement cycle for securities transactions from two days to one day, aiming to reduce various risks and improve operational efficiencies in the market.

dad6b45223d818960361be4c.title: Statement on the Proposed Shortening of the Settlement Cycle
dad6b45223d818960361be4c.speaker: Caroline A. Crenshaw

enrichment.summary: Caroline A. Crenshaw discusses the importance of shortening the securities settlement cycle to T+1, emphasizing its potential to reduce risks and enhance market efficiency while acknowledging associated costs. She also expresses interest in future advancements towards T+0 settlement.

5edea92aa4c2d6390cd34912.title: Statement on Cybersecurity Reforms in the Investment Management Industry
5edea92aa4c2d6390cd34912.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: SEC Chairman Gary Gensler supports comprehensive cybersecurity reforms aimed at enhancing risk management for registered investment advisers and companies. The proposed rules intend to improve cybersecurity preparedness, incident reporting, and overall resilience against threats, ultimately benefiting investors.

90a945fdc6225580ba0fd7cc.title: Statement on Cybersecurity Risk Management for Investment Advisers, Registered Investment Companies, and Business Development Companies
90a945fdc6225580ba0fd7cc.speaker: Allison Herren

enrichment.summary: The SEC addresses the rising cybersecurity threats and proposes a comprehensive framework for investment advisers and funds to enhance investor protection and market integrity. Key provisions include the requirement for written cybersecurity policies and incident notification protocols.

1e5e01369e8618397a1009d2.title: Statement on Cybersecurity Risk Management Proposal for Investment Advisers, Registered Investment Companies, and Business Development Companies
1e5e01369e8618397a1009d2.speaker: Caroline A. Crenshaw

enrichment.summary: In her speech, Caroline A. Crenshaw addresses the significant threat of cyberattacks on U.S. financial services firms, emphasizing the need for robust cybersecurity measures among investment advisers and funds. She supports a proposed rule requiring these entities to establish cybersecurity policies, report incidents, and inform investors about risks. The intention is to safeguard investor assets and maintain market stability.

7a9cb8d52a707ae152c8e16f.title: Statement on Private Fund Advisers Proposal
7a9cb8d52a707ae152c8e16f.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: Gary Gensler expresses support for proposed amendments to the Investment Advisers Act aimed at enhancing the transparency, efficiency, and competition among private fund advisers, which is crucial for protecting investors and fostering economic growth.

5f9a8d8102cda22ae63b9d87.title: Statement on Proposed Private Fund Advisers; Documentation of Investment Adviser Compliance Reviews Rulemaking
5f9a8d8102cda22ae63b9d87.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce expresses opposition to the SEC's proposed rulemaking on private fund advisers, arguing that it diverts attention and resources from protecting retail investors to wealthy private fund investors. She believes these investors can manage themselves and warns that the proposal may hinder capital formation and innovation.

56a50f710244dab615152e6c.title: Private Fund Advisers Proposal – Statement in Support of Accountability Enhancing Updates
56a50f710244dab615152e6c.speaker: Caroline A. Crenshaw

enrichment.summary: Caroline A. Crenshaw supports updates to enhance accountability for private fund advisers, emphasizing the fiduciary duty of advisers to prioritize client interests. She addresses concerns about opaque markets and proposes reforms for better disclosures to protect investors.

stance.label: supportive
stance.target: proposed reforms for private fund advisers

f90b16e69e1f1c55864d9348.title: Statement on Proposed Rules for Private Fund Advisers
f90b16e69e1f1c55864d9348.speaker: Allison Herren

enrichment.summary: Allison Herren supports proposed rules aimed at enhancing transparency, accountability, and reducing conflicts of interest in the private fund sector, impacting over $18 trillion in assets and retail investors.

stance.label: supportive
stance.target: proposed rules for private fund advisers

53812e28511e7966230e00ec.title: Statement before the Financial Stability Oversight Council on Money Market Funds, Open-End Bond Funds, and Hedge Funds
53812e28511e7966230e00ec.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: Gary Gensler emphasizes the importance of financial resiliency in money market funds, open-end bond funds, and hedge funds, highlighting their significant role in capital markets. He outlines potential risks to financial stability, the SEC's responsibilities, and ongoing efforts to enhance the resiliency of these fund sectors through proposed regulatory amendments.

Gary Gensler supports reopening the comment period for a proposed rule on corporate disclosure of 'pay versus performance' to enhance transparency in executive compensation linked to company performance.

stance.label: supportive
stance.target: proposed rule on pay versus performance

6f79d1f273d03bd0d2decd48.title: Statement on the Reopening of Pay vs. Performance
6f79d1f273d03bd0d2decd48.speaker: Caroline A. Crenshaw

enrichment.summary: Caroline A. Crenshaw reaffirms the importance of transparency and accountability in executive pay practices, particularly in light of evolving links to ESG measures. She emphasizes the need for reopening comment periods for stakeholder input on compensation disclosures and highlights the critical role of meaningful disclosures for investor decision-making.

f8b33d41c1a533c179787f69.title: Measuring Pay Against Performance: Are Shareholders Getting Their Money’s Worth?
f8b33d41c1a533c179787f69.speaker: Allison Herren

enrichment.summary: Allison Herren discusses the importance of linking executive compensation to company performance for investor evaluation. She highlights the long delays in implementing Dodd-Frank's disclosure rules and the need for updated metrics, including ESG goals, in executive pay assessments. The SEC's reopening of the comment period aims to gather feedback on proposed changes, particularly regarding smaller reporting companies and the flexibility of performance metrics.

65360c62137405bbf2e2df3e.title: Dissenting Statement on Reopening of Comment Period for Pay Versus Performance
65360c62137405bbf2e2df3e.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce expresses dissent regarding the approach taken in reopening the comment period for the Pay Versus Performance rule, criticizing it for failing to address past shortcomings and for proposing additional burdensome disclosure requirements.

4dc4b422779bffe777b57dc7.title: Statement on Government Securities Alternative Trading Systems
4dc4b422779bffe777b57dc7.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: Gary Gensler supports amendments to include significant Treasury market platforms within Regulation ATS, aiming to enhance resilience and access in the Treasury market. The proposal modernizes definitions and promotes transparency in trading.

entities.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve

8ebd3275ea34ebee741e1ef5.title: Dissenting Statement on the Proposal to Amend Regulation ATS
8ebd3275ea34ebee741e1ef5.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce expresses skepticism towards a proposal to amend Regulation ATS, emphasizing the need for careful consideration and an extended comment period to address key issues in the U.S. Treasury market.

6d8fcbd06b24f82cb0a265f0.title: Statement on Amendments to Exchange Act Rule 3b-16, Regulation ATS, and Regulation SCI
6d8fcbd06b24f82cb0a265f0.speaker: Caroline A. Crenshaw

enrichment.summary: Caroline A. Crenshaw discusses proposed amendments to enhance regulatory oversight for alternative trading systems (ATSs) to ensure fair competition among trading venues and improve investor protection. The amendments aim to close regulatory gaps and enhance operational transparency, particularly for ATSs trading government securities.

Gary Gensler supports amendments to Form PF to enhance regulatory oversight and assess systemic risk in private funds, emphasizing the need for timely reporting and addressing identified information gaps.

a90e3f732e199749f40fac9a.title: Statement on Proposed Amendments to Form PF to Require Current Reporting and Amend Reporting Requirements for Large Private Equity Advisers and Large Liquidity Fund Advisers
a90e3f732e199749f40fac9a.speaker: Hester M. Peirce

enrichment.summary: Hester M. Peirce expresses fundamental objections to the SEC's proposed amendments to Form PF, arguing that they shift its original purpose of assisting FSOC in monitoring systemic risk. She warns that the amendments would lead to unnecessary regulatory oversight and may harm smaller private equity advisers. Peirce advocates for raising, rather than lowering, the reporting threshold for large private equity advisers.

05357dacf378a7feb037ae13.title: Statement on Proposed Amendments to Form PF
05357dacf378a7feb037ae13.speaker: Allison Herren

enrichment.summary: The SEC has proposed amendments to Form PF to enhance investor protection and improve systemic risk monitoring in the growing private fund sector, which now manages over $11.7 trillion. The amendments require timely reporting of significant events affecting funds, improving transparency and regulatory oversight.

54532a420a6ca8d43a2db11f.title: Statement on Amendments to Form PF to Require Current Reporting and Amend Reporting Requirements for Large Private Equity Advisers and Large Liquidity Fund Advisers
54532a420a6ca8d43a2db11f.speaker: Caroline A. Crenshaw

enrichment.summary: Caroline A. Crenshaw discusses proposed amendments to Form PF aimed at improving data collection and oversight of private equity advisers and liquidity funds. The changes seek to enhance visibility into market risks and protect investors.

b9d0159be06af913920e5bd5.title: Statement on the Market Volatility Experienced in January 2021
b9d0159be06af913920e5bd5.speaker: Gary Gensler

enrichment.summary: Gary Gensler addressed the market volatility of January 2021, emphasizing the SEC's ongoing efforts to enhance fairness and efficiency in equity markets. He noted that staff findings and public comments will inform future recommendations.

"Legal representative" is limited to non‑professional representatives (e.g., non‑professional trustees, executors, conservators, POA holders), while regulated professionals (e.g., RIAs, broker‑dealers, banks, insurance companies) acting in that capacity are excluded. 2f701eeab479e4c1a06e1152.title: Staff Guidance on Automated Quotations under Regulation NMS
2f701eeab479e4c1a06e1152.speaker: Division of Trading and Markets

enrichment.summary: The SEC Division of Trading and Markets staff provides guidance on what constitutes a de minimis intentional access delay for purposes of determining whether a trading center maintains an "automated quotation" under Rule 600(b)(3) and Rule 611 of Regulation NMS. While the Commission's June 17, 2016 interpretation allows de minimis intentional delays without defining a specific threshold, the staff states that intentional access delays of less than one millisecond are de minimis in today's market environment. Such delays are seen as consistent with the requirement that quotations be "immediate," because they fall within typical geographic and technological latencies experienced when routing orders between trading centers. The staff emphasizes that this is non-binding guidance, does not guarantee Commission approval of any particular delay or rule filing, and does not mean that all delays at or above one millisecond are necessarily non–de minimis. All proposed intentional access delays must still be filed with the Commission as rule changes, and the staff will revisit this guidance as technology and market conditions evolve.

stance.label: supportive
stance.target: Use of sub-millisecond intentional access delays as consistent with "immediate" automated quotations under Regulation NMS

bad459b78f82ce21f42591d3.speaker: Division of Trading and Markets

enrichment.summary: The SEC Division of Trading and Markets reiterates that broker-dealers relying on the Securities Act Section 4(a)(4) exemption for unregistered customer sales must conduct a fact-specific, "reasonable inquiry" into each transaction to ensure the customer's sale is exempt from Section 5 registration. Section 4(a)(4) protects only the broker's part of the transaction and is unavailable where the broker-dealer knows or has reasonable grounds to believe the customer's sale is not exempt (e.g., the customer is an underwriter or the sale is part of a distribution). The FAQ outlines potential exemptions (Sections 4(a)(4) and 4(a)(3)), details the elements of reasonable inquiry (tracking Rule 144(g)(4) Note (ii)), emphasizes heightened "searching" inquiry where red flags appear (e.g., large blocks of recently issued shares of little-known issuers, rapid resales, repeat transactions, new issuers, or customer stock promotion), and clarifies that DTC eligibility or the absence of restrictive legends do not relieve brokers of their inquiry obligations or the need for a valid exemption from registration.

The FAQs emphasize that the Exchange Act does not presume compliance or legal personnel are supervisors of business-line employees solely due to their roles. Whether an individual is a "supervisor" is a fact-specific inquiry focused on whether the person has the requisite responsibility, ability, or authority to affect another employee's conduct, including explicit or implicit delegation of supervisory authority. The guidance clarifies that providing advice, counseling, remediation assistance, participating in management or other committees, or consulting with senior management, by itself, does not create supervisory status. Broker-dealers can and should build robust compliance programs that include monitoring, escalation, and clearly delineated supervisory responsibilities residing with business-line management, so that compliance/legal functions remain advisory where intended. It also explains operational requirements for chaperoning arrangements, including confirmation delivery, recordkeeping, capital requirements, treatment of failed trades, and the 30‑day limit for unchaperoned in‑person visits. The staff expands and applies the definition of "major U.S. institutional investor" across Rule 15a-6, including entities wholly owned by such investors, while emphasizing that solicitation analysis is fact‑specific and that chaperoning broker-dealers retain ultimate U.S. regulatory responsibility.

b264743e1f4b82f9c611ed20.title: Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act: Frequently Asked Questions About Crowdfunding Intermediaries
b264743e1f4b82f9c611ed20.speaker: Division of Trading and Markets

enrichment.summary: The SEC Division of Trading and Markets provides guidance on the implementation of Title III of the JOBS Act as it applies to crowdfunding intermediaries, clarifying registration requirements, the definition and limitations of funding portals, and the core legal and compliance obligations of crowdfunding brokers and funding portals. The FAQs emphasize that intermediaries must register with the SEC (as brokers or funding portals) and become members of a national securities association (currently FINRA), and that no one may act as a crowdfunding intermediary until the SEC completes rulemaking. Funding portals are strictly limited in their activities (no investment advice, solicitation, transaction-based compensation for sales, or handling of investor funds), and are subject to extensive investor protection duties, including providing educational materials, risk disclosures, fraud-reduction measures, and ensuring compliance with investment limits and offering conditions. The document is explanatory and neutral, describing obligations and restrictions without expressing policy preferences, and noting that the FAQs themselves are not formal SEC rules or approvals.

297780acfc92ee862b141a9d.title: Division of Trading and Market Guidance Regarding Sale of Loaned But Recalled Securities
297780acfc92ee862b141a9d.speaker: Division of Trading and Markets

enrichment.summary: The SEC Division of Trading and Markets clarifies that when a person has loaned out a security and subsequently sells that security, the sale may be treated as a "long" sale under the Commission's 2008 Emergency Orders if a bona fide recall of the loaned security is initiated within two business days after the trade date. In that case, the lender is deemed to own the security for purposes of Rule 200(g)(1) and Rule 200(b) of Regulation SHO, and the sale is not treated as a short sale for: (1) Form SH reporting of new short sales, (2) the order halting short selling in financial stocks, and (3) Rule 204T related to protection against naked short selling abuses. Broker-dealers may mark such orders as "long" if they also comply with Rule 200(c) of Regulation SHO, and the long-sale close-out requirement in Rule 204T applies.

enrichment.summary: The U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts entered a final judgment against investment adviser Jeffrey Cutter and his firm, Cutter Financial Group LLC (CFG), for breaching fiduciary duties in connection with annuity sales to advisory clients. Following an April 23, 2025 jury verdict, the court ordered CFG to pay a $100,000 civil penalty and Cutter to pay a $50,000 civil penalty. The judgment requires Cutter and CFG to provide a copy of the judgment to all existing and new advisory clients for five years and enjoins them, for the same period, from future violations of Section 206(2) of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940. The jury had found them liable for violating Section 206(2) but found in their favor on the SEC’s claims under Sections 206(1) and 206(4) and Rule 206(4)-7, which related to inadequate disclosure of financial incentives for recommending fixed index annuities over other investments. The SEC’s case was handled by staff in the Boston Regional Office.

Gessin was additionally barred from participating in most securities activities, prohibited from serving as an officer or director of a public company, and ordered to pay a $945,804 civil penalty. enrichment.summary: The SEC filed and settled civil charges against investment adviser Marat Likhtenstein for operating a self-issued promissory note scheme that raised over $4.1 million from at least 15 advisory clients, many elderly and primarily from the Russian-American Jewish community. The complaint alleges that from 2017 to 2024 he falsely promised extraordinary returns from lucrative business opportunities but did not invest client funds, instead misappropriating them, including $940,000 in Ponzi-like payments and nearly $3.2 million for personal expenses. The SEC charged violations of antifraud provisions of the Securities Act, Exchange Act, and Investment Advisers Act, seeking disgorgement, prejudgment interest, civil penalties, and conduct-based and anti-fraud injunctions. Likhtenstein consented, without admitting or denying the allegations, to a bifurcated settlement providing for injunctive relief, with monetary remedies to be decided later; the court entered the consent judgment on February 4, 2026. A parallel criminal case was brought by the Kings County District Attorney’s Office, and the SEC acknowledges that office’s assistance.

enrichment.summary: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Ohio announced that former Cleveland VA Medical Center logistics employee Dustin Jagger and accomplice Damarco McKinley were each sentenced to 12 months and 1 day in prison and three years of supervised release for a scheme involving nearly $200,000 in fraudulent purchases on a government-issued credit card. Jagger used his VA-issued card to buy $198,183.84 in iPads, iPhones, and other electronics and goods, some of which he kept and others he resold online, including to McKinley. McKinley was stopped in Indiana en route to Chicago with over $29,000 in VA-purchased electronics and other items, including a handgun, loaded magazine, credit cards in others' names, and cash. Jagger was ordered to pay $198,183.84 in restitution, with $29,124.56 joint and several with McKinley. DOJ and VA OIG officials emphasized that the conduct eroded public trust and misused taxpayer funds intended for veterans, and noted that the case was investigated by the VA Office of Inspector General and prosecuted by an Assistant U.S. Attorney.

A joint FBI and NCIS investigation linked the channel and videos, which included purported imagery of Department of Defense facilities, critical national security infrastructure, and locations labeled as "classified" or "Top Secret," to Bennett through IP address data, recovery phone numbers, and USPS-registered email addresses. A subsequent search of Bennett's residence resulted in the seizure of a Potensic Atom drone, micro-SD cards, and a computer system, including a monitor displaying the YouTube channel logged in; at least one SD card allegedly contained video of a drone flight over the Raven Rock Mountain Complex. The case highlights federal enforcement of airspace restrictions around national defense installations and collaboration between the FBI, NCIS, and Pentagon Force Protection Agency.

enrichment.summary: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Michigan announced that Garber Management Group, Inc., affiliated with the Garber Automotive Group, will pay $1,513,281 to settle civil allegations under the False Claims Act that it obtained a Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loan for which it was ineligible. The government alleges Garber falsely certified eligibility for an $864,732 first-draw PPP loan and forgiveness by not properly aggregating its employees with affiliates, which would have exceeded the 500-employee limit, and that it did not qualify for an exemption as a franchise with an SBA franchise identifier code. The settlement arises from a sealed qui tam whistleblower case, U.S. ex rel. David Reed v. Garber Management, Inc., in which the whistleblower will receive 10% of the recovery. The matter was handled by Assistant U.S. Attorney Leslie Wizner with support from the SBA’s Office of General Counsel. DOJ encourages the public to report suspected COVID-19 fraud to the National Center for Disaster Fraud. The settlement resolves allegations only, with no determination of liability.

enrichment.summary: Governor Michael S. Barr argues that artificial intelligence, particularly generative AI, is likely to be a general-purpose technology with substantial long-run benefits for productivity, innovation, and living standards, but with potentially painful short-run disruptions for specific worker groups and sectors. He outlines three scenarios for AI's evolution: (1) gradual diffusion with strong but manageable productivity gains and limited, temporary joblessness; (2) a rapid "jobless boom" with widespread displacement, rising unemployment, and major distributional and social challenges; and (3) stalled progress and overinvestment, where AI's productivity impact is modest and risks shift toward financial stress. Powell announces that the Department of Justice has served the Federal Reserve with grand jury subpoenas threatening a criminal indictment related to his June Senate testimony on a multi-year renovation of historic Fed office buildings. Powell asserts respect for the rule of law and accountability, but characterizes the subpoenas as an unprecedented action that must be viewed in the broader context of administration threats and pressure. He argues that the stated focus on his testimony and building renovations is a pretext, and that the real issue is retaliation for the Fed setting interest rates according to evidence and economic conditions rather than the President's preferences. Powell frames the situation as a test of whether monetary policy will remain independent or be directed by political pressure or intimidation. He notes his service under four administrations of both parties and reaffirms his intention to continue performing his duties, emphasizing integrity, independence, and the Fed's mandate of price stability and maximum employment.

Waller reflects on how John Taylor’s work on rules versus discretion in monetary policy, and specifically Taylor’s 1983 commentary on Barro and Gordon, inspired Waller’s own 20‑year research program on central bank institutional design. He traces the evolution from Kydland and Prescott’s time‑inconsistency problem and Barro–Gordon’s reputation model, through Rogoff’s argument for a more inflation‑averse ("conservative") central banker and Alesina’s partisan business cycles, to Waller’s own work on central bank boards with staggered, long, and independent terms. Waller argues that credibility is more robust when embedded in institutions rather than in individuals, and that an independent, board‑based central bank structure—like the Federal Reserve’s Board of Governors—can balance democratic accountability (via appointments) with macroeconomic stability (via insulation from short‑term political pressures). He credits John Taylor’s single line about society finding institutional solutions to time inconsistency for launching his research journey and closes by affirming the value and durability of the Fed’s current governance model.

enrichment.summary: Governor Adriana D. Kugler delivered an economics lecture at Harvard University on April 7, 2025, explaining recent U.S. inflation dynamics and the role of the Phillips curve in modeling them. She describes pandemic-era inflation as occurring in waves—first food, then core goods, then core services, and finally housing—and links these patterns to sector-specific factors such as shortages, demand rotation to goods, wages, and housing rents. The lecture then uses the Phillips curve framework, including wage and expectations-augmented versions, to analyze how inflation relates to labor market slack, expectations, and other drivers. Kugler reviews empirical results across different periods (1960–1986 vs. 1987–2019), presents a baseline and updated Phillips curve models, and shows dynamic simulations, including models that incorporate the vacancy-to-unemployment ratio and measures of shortages, in an effort to better capture the most recent inflation episode.

Governor Michael S. Barr outlines how generative AI (Gen AI), banks, and fintechs intersect, emphasizing that Gen AI could become a competitive necessity in banking but must be integrated responsibly. He argues that banking is inherently data-driven and that Gen AI can improve document analysis, credit underwriting, customer service via advanced chatbots, and trading/analytics. Despite this potential, banks have moved cautiously due to model immaturity (hallucinations, stochastic outputs), strict requirements for precision and explainability, information-security and privacy risks, and internal tech debt and siloed data.

Barr contrasts fintechs’ speed, clean tech stacks, and single-product focus with banks’ scale, rich customer data, diversified business lines, and mature risk controls. He frames the bank–fintech dynamic as a race between speed (fintechs) and scale (banks), suggesting that both competition and collaboration (e.g., partnerships, investments, vendor relationships) will likely accelerate Gen AI adoption in financial services. This acceleration, he argues, can benefit consumers via better, cheaper, and faster financial services, provided that risks are well managed.

enrichment.summary: The Ethereum Foundation has begun staking 70,000 ETH from its treasury to generate rewards that will fund protocol research, ecosystem development, and community grants. The process started with a 2,016 ETH deposit and uses Dirk and Vouch, open-source validator tools from Attestant, to distribute signing and validator duties across multiple jurisdictions and reduce single points of failure. This move follows the public release of the Foundation's treasury policy, which aims to balance long-term financial sustainability with Ethereum-aligned values such as decentralization, open-source access, and user privacy. The staking setup combines hosted infrastructure and self-managed hardware, including minority clients, deployed in several countries. With an estimated staking yield of around 2.808% according to the CoinDesk Composite Ether Staking Rate (CESR), the Foundation is putting a portion of its roughly 172,650 ETH (plus 10,000 WETH) holdings to productive use rather than leaving them idle.

68df1bce679a8ba9099f2bb6.speaker: FINRA

enrichment.summary: FINRA, as part of its FINRA Forward modernization initiative, has amended Rule 3220 (the Gifts Rule) effective March 30, 2026. The amendments raise the annual gift limit from $100 to $300 per recipient, codify and clarify prior interpretive guidance, and authorize exemptive relief. New supplementary material defines valuation and aggregation standards, clarifies supervision and recordkeeping obligations, and delineates categories of gifts that are excluded from the $300 cap and recordkeeping requirements: personal gifts for infrequent life events, bereavement gifts, de minimis and logo promotional items, commemorative items commemorating a business transaction (even if over $300), and certain disaster-relief donations. The rule is confirmed not to apply to gifts to a member’s own associated persons or to individual retail customers. FINRA also adopts conforming $300 gift limits in Rules 2310, 2320, 2341, and 5110, aiming to modernize the regulatory framework while maintaining investor protection and providing flexible, risk-based supervisory expectations.

48901e0731c128a96978adf3.speaker: FINRA

enrichment.summary: FINRA alerts member firms that misapplication of ASC 606 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers) in recognizing fees from customer contracts has led to violations of SEA Rules 15c3-1 (Net Capital), 17a-3 (Recordkeeping), and 17a-5 (Financial Reporting). Examinations found firms prematurely recognizing non-refundable M&A fees as revenue without performing or documenting the ASC 606-required performance obligation analysis, causing overstated revenues, understated liabilities and non-allowable assets, and in some cases net capital deficiencies or material reductions in excess net capital. 32dc762fcfeef50367ddf579.speaker: FINRA

enrichment.summary: FINRA permanently amends several procedural rules to allow the Office of Hearing Officers (OHO) and the National Adjudicatory Council (NAC) to conduct evidentiary and oral argument hearings by video conference under specified conditions, expanding prior temporary COVID-19 measures. In-person hearings remain the default, but OHO and NAC may now order video hearings sua sponte when in‑person proceedings would endanger health or safety or be impracticable (e.g., natural disasters, terrorism), and may also act on party motions. For NAC oral arguments, video conferences may also be ordered for other reasons, subject to parties showing any material disadvantage from remote format. The amendments apply to disciplinary, membership, eligibility, funding portal eligibility, TCDO/PCDO proceedings, and NAC appeals, and become effective August 23, 2023.

enrichment.summary: FINRA Regulatory Notice 23-11 seeks public comment on a concept proposal for new FINRA Rule 4610, which would establish liquidity risk management requirements for certain broker-dealers, primarily large carrying and clearing firms and those meeting Supplemental Liquidity Schedule (SLS) thresholds. The contemplated rule would require covered members to maintain a formal Liquidity Risk Management Program (LRMP), conduct regular liquidity stress tests (LSTs) over a 30‑day horizon, maintain and use a contingency funding plan (CFP), and at all times have sufficient cash or liquid assets to meet obligations as they come due. 60ace27e90a5b7b2fe37059d.speaker: FINRA

enrichment.summary: FINRA has amended Rule 8312 (FINRA BrokerCheck Disclosure), effective June 1, 2023, to require public disclosure on BrokerCheck of whether a current or former member firm is designated as a "Restricted Firm" under Rules 4111 (Restricted Firm Obligations) and 9561 (Procedures for Regulating Activities Under Rule 4111). Rule 4111 establishes an annual, multi-step process to identify firms with a significant history of misconduct that pose a high degree of risk to investors and to impose a Restricted Deposit Requirement and/or operational conditions or restrictions on such firms. Rule 9561 provides expedited procedures to implement Rule 4111, and a firm’s Restricted Firm designation remains effective and visible on BrokerCheck during any related expedited proceeding, with an indication when the designation is on appeal. The change aims to enhance investor protection by alerting investors to the Restricted Firm status on both summary and detailed BrokerCheck reports and to further incentivize high-risk firms to change behaviors to avoid or remove such designation.

a3bf8d9b987bc51b85b0b795.speaker: FINRA

enrichment.summary: FINRA Regulatory Notice 23-06 highlights a rising trend in fraudulent transfers of customer accounts through the Automated Customer Account Transfer Service (ACATS). stance.target: Enhanced supervisory, identity verification, and fraud reporting practices to mitigate ACATS-related fraud risk.

If the SEC adopts the amendments, proprietary trading firms currently relying on Rule 15b9-1 would generally be required to register with FINRA, making FINRA’s existing fee structure, including the Trading Activity Fee (TAF), applicable to them. Regulatory Notice 15-13 had proposed an exemption from the TAF for transactions by proprietary trading firms on exchanges of which they are members, and FINRA now seeks renewed public comment on whether this exemption (or alternatives such as a different TAF rate for proprietary firms) is appropriate, equitable across members, and what economic, competitive, and behavioral impacts it may have on trading patterns, liquidity, and market functioning.

Foreign sovereign debt securities are defined as debt issued or guaranteed by a foreign government, its political subdivisions (including state, provincial, or municipal governments), or supranational entities. These trades must be reported on a same-day or next-business-day (T+1, as/of) basis depending on execution time, but will not be publicly disseminated. FAQs clarify that only securities issued in U.S. dollars qualify, that reporting is required even where only ISIN/FIGI is available (via a TRACE New Issue Form), and that foreign municipal debt issued in U.S. dollars is included.

enrichment.summary: FINRA seeks public comment on proposed amendments to TRACE Rule 6730 to create a two-part reporting regime for delayed Treasury spot trades in corporate debt. Currently, such trades are only reported to TRACE once the dollar price is known, even though the key economic terms (spread to a benchmark U.S. Treasury and other terms) may have been agreed hours earlier.
